text:
Erin: quick sync — i'm kicking off a tiny experiment for cross-region shard-signalling (working name: shard-signal). goal: keep active/active low-latency for local reads/writes while satisfying per-tenant data residency flags. thinking soft leases + client region hints. thoughts?

James: +1 to soft leases. key tradeoff is tail latency when primary local is saturated and we fallback to remote. we should avoid synchronous cross-region commits. prefer best-effort local commit and async reconciliation for non-PII. :thinking:

Li: can we standardize a routing header for this? propose `x-shard-pref: region=eu-west-1;score=0.9` so proxies can prefer region without hard pinning. also add `x-shard-lease` for lease metadata so proxies and workers can read without extra control-plane calls.

Sofia: important — for tenants with strict residency we need hard rejects, not fallbacks. also encryption keys for those tenants must never leave region (KMS in-region). otherwise fallback is illegal. we need a tenant-level residency enum: HARD_LOCAL | SOFT_LOCAL | GLOBAL.

Erin: agreed on enum. experiment will only run for SOFT_LOCAL tenants. rough lease header i'm testing:
```
Lease: shard=shard-42; epoch=125; region=eu-west-1; ttl=3s; sig=sha256:...;
X-Shard-Pref: region=eu-west-1;score=0.95
```

James: TTL=3s seems reasonable for quick failover, but we should add jitter and backoff to avoid thundering. also record lease refresh latency metric (lease.refresh.p50/p95).

Li: proxy behavior proposal: prefer local while lease is valid; if 5xx or qps>threshold then route to next-best region using `score` order. when routing remote for writes, attach `X-Write-Origins: eu-west-1` so remote can tag and potential async mirror can later reconcile.

Sofia: +1 for write origin tag. for SOFT_LOCAL, ensure remote writes keep a short-lived escrow flag and a scheduled sweep to backfill primary when it returns. non-PII only.

Erin: ops-bot reminder: i'm going to canary this to 2% of SOFT_LOCAL tenants in eu-west-1 starting tomorrow at 09:30 UTC. will add metrics: regional-fallback-rate, avg-fallback-latency, reconciliation-delay, error-by-tenant-policy.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: shard-signal v0.1 -> canary (eu-west-1) at 2025-06-12 09:30 UTC. will notify on completion. :rocket:

James: risk note — KV cache ownership: if remote handles write, we must invalidate prefix cache in local region or serve stale reads. propose per-shard prefix version tag in responses so caches can detect mismatch. small header: `x-prefix-v=20250612-01`

Li: i'll add proxy metrics and a tiny middleware to emit `x-prefix-v` and watch for mismatches. i'll own canary dashboard.

Sofia: also add an auditor job to scan SOFT_LOCAL tenants for any key material leaving region — quick smoke check after canary. i'll add to runbook.

Erin: ok plan: (1) canary 2% SOFT_LOCAL tomorrow, (2) monitor metrics Li adds, (3) runbook readiness from Sofia, (4) roll if fallback-rate <0.5% and reconciliation-delay < 60s. James/Li/Sofia — thanks, i'll post results in #architecture after the canary. :+1:

James: cool. one final thought — let's keep the lease arbitration logic in the data-plane proxy, not control plane, to reduce control-plane latency coupling.

Erin: agreed, proxy-based arbitration for now. follow-ups: Li will push proxy changes, James will add prefix tag, Sofia will draft runbook. i'll coordinate the canary window.

Li: got it, will PR today.

Sofia: drafting runbook now.

ops-bot: canary started: shard-signal v0.1 at 2025-06-12 09:30 UTC (2% SOFT_LOCAL). monitoring channels: #infra-metrics, #oncall.

Erin: thanks everyone — keeping this limited and observable. will reopen thread with canary numbers.
